lines.text: And Freddie Mac's average 30-year mortgage rate jumped to 7.28%, up from 7.11% a week earlier.

lines.text: Chapter 1: Six days of red.

lines.text: On Thursday, the S&P 500 fell 2%, to 7,175.83, its sixth loss in a row.
lines.say: On Thursday, the S and P five hundred fell two percent, to seven thousand one hundred seventy-five point eight three, its sixth loss in a row.

lines.text: That's its longest losing streak since 2024. The Dow dropped 1,101 points, and the Nasdaq fell 2.3%.
lines.say: That's its longest losing streak since twenty twenty-four. The Dow dropped one thousand one hundred one points, and the Nasdaq fell two point three percent.

lines.text: More than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell that day. This wasn't one bad company.
lines.say: More than ninety percent of S and P five hundred stocks fell that day. This wasn't one bad company.

lines.text: Here's the bigger picture: where the S&P 500 ended each year since 2021, plus where it closed on Thursday.
lines.say: Here's the bigger picture: where the S and P five hundred ended each year since twenty twenty-one, plus where it closed on Thursday.

lines.text: In 2022, when the Fed was raising rates fast, the index fell about 19%, and bonds lost money that year too.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-two, when the Fed was raising rates fast, the index fell about nineteen percent, and bonds lost money that year too.

lines.text: After that came three strong years in a row, ending with 2025 up about 16% for the year.
lines.say: After that came three strong years in a row, ending with twenty twenty-five up about sixteen percent for the year.

lines.text: So even after this slide, it was still up about 4.8% for 2026 as of Thursday's close. That's our math.

lines.text: The mood around AI soured. The question is whether the enormous sums being spent on it will ever pay off.
lines.say: The mood around AI soured. The question is whether the enormous sums being spent on it will ever pay off.

lines.text: Look at Nvidia, the company selling the chips. On Tuesday it reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion.
lines.say: Look at Nvidia, the company selling the chips. On Tuesday it reported record quarterly revenue of one hundred fifteen point eight billion dollars.

lines.text: That's up 103% from a year earlier, and above the $109.1 billion analysts expected.
lines.say: That's up one hundred three percent from a year earlier, and above the one hundred nine point one billion dollars analysts expected.

lines.text: That's a clear beat, by about $6.7 billion, by our math. On paper, it was a blowout quarter.
lines.say: That's a clear beat, by about six point seven billion dollars, by our math. On paper, it was a blowout quarter.

lines.text: It also guided next quarter's sales to about $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.
lines.say: It also guided next quarter's sales to about one hundred thirty billion dollars, plus or minus three percent.

lines.text: And yet the stock slipped on Wednesday, then fell again on Thursday after an early jump faded.
lines.say: And yet the stock slipped on Wednesday, then fell again on Thursday after an early jump faded.

lines.text: Investors were also digesting a leadership shock: longtime CEO Jensen Huang's sudden exit.
lines.say: Investors were also digesting a leadership shock: longtime CEO Jensen Huang's sudden exit.

lines.text: When the biggest AI chip company beats and still drops, the market is asking for proof, not promises.
lines.say: When the biggest AI chip company beats and still drops, the market is asking for proof, not promises.

lines.text: Chapter 2: The Fed isn't done.
lines.say: Chapter two: The Fed isn't done.

lines.text: Now the second half of the story. On Wednesday, the Fed released minutes from its October meeting.
lines.say: Now the second half of the story. On Wednesday, the Fed released minutes from its October meeting.

lines.text: First, a quick rewind. In September, the Fed raised rates for the first time since July 2023.
lines.say: First, a quick rewind. In September, the Fed raised rates for the first time since July twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: That quarter-point hike put its key rate at 3.75% to 4%. In October, it held there.
lines.say: That quarter-point hike put its key rate at three point seven five to four percent. In October, it held there.

lines.text: Here's that rate at the end of each year since 2021, using the top of the range. It's been a roller coaster.
lines.say: Here's that rate at the end of each year since twenty twenty-one, using the top of the range. It's been a roller coaster.

lines.text: It peaked at 5.5% in 2023. Then the Fed cut rates in 2024 and 2025, down to 3.75%.
lines.say: It peaked at five and a half percent in twenty twenty-three. Then the Fed cut rates in twenty twenty-four and twenty twenty-five, down to three point seven five percent.

lines.text: Now it's climbing again, to 4%, because inflation came back. September prices were up 3.7% from a year earlier.
lines.say: Now it's climbing again, to four percent, because inflation came back. September prices were up three point seven percent from a year earlier.

lines.text: Is the Fed done? The minutes say probably not.
lines.say: Is the Fed done? The minutes say probably not.

lines.text: Almost all officials judged that further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate.
lines.say: Almost all officials judged that further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate.

lines.text: In plain English: almost every official at the table expects more rate hikes.
lines.say: In plain English: almost every official at the table expects more rate hikes.

lines.text: A couple of officials even said a hike bigger than a quarter point could be considered in December, if inflation data look bad.
lines.say: A couple of officials even said a hike bigger than a quarter point could be considered in December, if inflation data look bad.

lines.text: The October vote to hold was 10 to 2. The two dissenters, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, wanted a hike right away.
lines.say: The October vote to hold was ten to two. The two dissenters, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, wanted a hike right away.

lines.text: Now here's the thread I promised. The minutes say many officials see the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk.
lines.say: Now here's the thread I promised. The minutes say many officials see the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk.

lines.text: A data center needs chips, electricity, steel and land, and workers. All that demand can push prices up.
lines.say: A data center needs chips, electricity, steel and land, and workers. All that demand can push prices up.

lines.text: Fed staff also flagged a risk in how some AI companies finance each other, in case the payoff disappoints.
lines.say: Fed staff also flagged a risk in how some AI companies finance each other, in case the payoff disappoints.

lines.text: So AI is doing two jobs at once: it's shaking stock prices, and it's giving the Fed a reason to keep rates high.
lines.say: So AI is doing two jobs at once: it's shaking stock prices, and it's giving the Fed a reason to keep rates high.

lines.text: That's how a story about computer chips ends up inside your mortgage payment.

lines.text: Chapter 3: Why rates rose anyway.
lines.say: Chapter three: Why rates rose anyway.

lines.text: Remember the usual pattern: stocks fall, investors buy bonds, yields drop, and loans get cheaper.
lines.say: Remember the usual pattern: stocks fall, investors buy bonds, yields drop, and loans get cheaper.

lines.text: On Thursday, that sort of happened. The 10-year Treasury yield slipped a little, to 5.04%.
lines.say: On Thursday, that sort of happened. The ten-year Treasury yield slipped a little, to five point oh four percent.

lines.text: But look at that level. In September, the 10-year topped 5% for the first time since 2007.
lines.say: But look at that level. In September, the ten-year topped five percent for the first time since two thousand seven.

lines.text: Why so high? Inflation is above the Fed's 2% goal, and bond buyers expect more hikes, so they demand more.
lines.say: Why so high? Inflation is above the Fed's two percent goal, and bond buyers expect more hikes, so they demand more.

lines.text: The 2-year Treasury yield shows those hike bets. It closed Thursday at 4.76%, well above the Fed's 4% top rate.
lines.say: The two-year Treasury yield shows those hike bets. It closed Thursday at four point seven six percent, well above the Fed's four percent top rate.

lines.text: When the 2-year sits that far above the Fed's rate, traders are betting short-term rates are headed higher.
lines.say: When the two-year sits that far above the Fed's rate, traders are betting short-term rates are headed higher.

lines.text: And here's the key: mortgage rates follow long-term bond yields, not the Fed's rate directly.
lines.say: And here's the key: mortgage rates follow long-term bond yields, not the Fed's rate directly.

lines.text: So Freddie Mac's 30-year rate jumped to 7.28% this week, ending a four-week slide.
lines.say: So Freddie Mac's thirty-year rate jumped to seven point two eight percent this week, ending a four-week slide.

lines.text: It had peaked at 7.40% on October 8th, then fell four weeks in a row, down to 7.11%.
lines.say: It had peaked at seven point four percent on October eighth, then fell four weeks in a row, down to seven point one one percent.

lines.text: This week's bounce erased more than half of that drop.
lines.say: This week's bounce erased more than half of that drop.

lines.text: Here's Freddie Mac's 30-year rate in the same week of November, every year since 2021.
lines.say: Here's Freddie Mac's thirty-year rate in the same week of November, every year since twenty twenty-one.

lines.text: Back in 2021, it was about 3.1%. Those days feel like a different planet.
lines.say: Back in twenty twenty-one, it was about three point one percent. Those days feel like a different planet.

lines.text: A year ago, it was 6.26%. Now it's more than a full point higher.
lines.say: A year ago, it was six point two six percent. Now it's more than a full point higher.

lines.text: On a $400,000 loan, monthly principal and interest goes from about $2,465 to about $2,737, by our math.
lines.say: On a four hundred thousand dollar loan, monthly principal and interest goes from about two thousand four hundred sixty-five dollars to about two thousand seven hundred thirty-seven, by our math.

lines.text: That's about $271 more every month, or more than $3,000 a year, for the same house.
lines.say: That's about two hundred seventy-one dollars more every month, or more than three thousand dollars a year, for the same house.

lines.text: Home builders feel it too. Their confidence index fell to 25 in November, the lowest since April 2012.
lines.say: Home builders feel it too. Their confidence index fell to twenty-five in November, the lowest since April twenty twelve.

lines.text: And 46% of builders cut prices this month, with an average cut of 6%.
lines.say: And forty-six percent of builders cut prices this month, with an average cut of six percent.

lines.text: So housing has a strange mix: some lower new-home prices, but pricier loans.
lines.say: So housing has a strange mix: some lower new-home prices, but pricier loans.

lines.text: Chapter 4: Shoppers kept spending.
lines.say: Chapter four: Shoppers kept spending.

lines.text: Here's a twist: while Wall Street sold off, big retailers had a decent week.
lines.say: Here's a twist: while Wall Street sold off, big retailers had a decent week.

lines.text: Walmart said revenue rose 5.2%, to $188.8 billion, and it raised its outlook for the third time this year.

lines.say: Target's comparable sales grew five point six percent, and Home Depot's sales rose four point nine percent, to forty-three point four billion dollars.

lines.text: But part of that boost doesn't come from shoppers at all. It comes from tariff refunds.
lines.say: But part of that boost doesn't come from shoppers at all. It comes from tariff refunds.

lines.text: In February, the Supreme Court struck down tariffs that were imposed under an emergency powers law called IEEPA.
lines.say: In February, the Supreme Court struck down tariffs that were imposed under an emergency powers law called I E E P A.

lines.text: So importers can get those tariffs refunded, and that money lands in their profits.
lines.say: So importers can get those tariffs refunded, and that money lands in their profits.

lines.say: Target's third quarter included three hundred one million dollars in tariff refund benefits, before taxes.

lines.say: Walmart said in August it had received about two point nine billion dollars in refunds, and planned to use them to cut prices.

lines.text: So who came out ahead? Savers earning higher yields and big retailers did better, while stock owners and home buyers took the hit.

lines.text: Second, credit cards. Most card rates are tied to the prime rate, which moves up with every Fed hike.

post.title: Stocks Fell 6 Days Straight. So Why Did Mortgage Rates Go Up?
post.ig: Stocks fell six days straight, yet mortgage rates jumped to 7.28%. Here's why, and what it means for you.
post.tiktok: Stocks fell 6 days straight. Mortgage rates rose anyway, to 7.28%. Here's the AI thread that ties it together.
post.yt_desc:
The S&P 500 fell six days in a row and, as of Thursday's close, sat 8.2% below its October record, as doubts about AI spending hit stocks even after Nvidia reported record revenue of $115.8 billion. In the same week, Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes, with many calling the AI buildout an inflation risk, and Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate jumped to 7.28%. This video explains why loan rates rose while stocks fell, who came out ahead and who took the hit, and what it means for your 401(k), credit cards, savings and home loans.
